title: I2C Bus Scanner
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Learning MicroPython
description: Slow-motion I2C address scan. The CPU asks every address from 0x08 to 0x77 and an MPU-6050 (0x68), an HMC5883L compass (0x1E) and an SSD1306 display (0x3C) answer with ACK. Shows the SCL and SDA waveforms, an address map and the console output of i2c-scanner.py.

learningObjectives: Explain how an I2C scan discovers devices: the controller asks each address and only the owner answers with an ACK
Read an I2C scan result such as [30, 60, 104] and name the devices in hex and decimal
Predict how a scan result changes when a device is unplugged

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Step-through with prediction, plus an unplug experiment
keyQuestions: Who sends the address, the CPU or the device?
What does the wire do during the ACK clock pulse when nobody is home?
Why can two devices on one bus not share an address?
commonMisconceptions: Devices announce their own addresses (the CPU asks; devices only answer)
Every device sees only its own address (all devices hear every address on the shared wires)
assessmentOpportunities: Student explains why a device does not announce itself
Student predicts the scan result after unplugging a device
